reason: 'Leaves 6–9' is a leaf count of 6–9.
The standard is the adaxial petal of a papilionoid flower, so petal + emarginate with '±' as approximately is right.
Peduncle length is 0.3–1.5 cm, as stated.

The lowest calyx lobe (sepal, with 'lower' FLOPO:0991377 as context) is narrowly linear-lanceolate. 'Lanceolate' is the head of the compound, and 'linear' and 'narrowly' only narrow it. The context slot keeps the statement true for the lowest lobe only.
Secondary veins number 10–14 on each side of the midvein, in the leaf, as stated.
The apex of the leaf blade is acuminate. Leaf lamina tip is the right bearer to swap in.
'Leaf solitary' means one leaf.
Branchlets are blackish gray when old. Bearer is branch, the value is gray, and old (PATO:0000308) is the state context. 'Blackish' only shades the gray.

target: oval-elliptic (PATO:0001877 lanceolate side wrong) — range from elliptic/oval to lanceolate-ovate
fix: In 'A-B to C-D' the hyphen joins a compound shape on each side of 'to'. The range runs from the first compound to the second. The hyphen inside 'lanceolate-ovate' is not its own range.
reason: The flora gives a range from oval-elliptic to lanceolate-ovate. The annotation turns the compound 'lanceolate-ovate' into a lanceolate-to-ovate range and drops the oval-elliptic end.
Leafy twigs are ± angular. Branch is a fair bearer for twigs.
Cauline leaves are carnose, which means fleshy. The basal leaves are carnose too, so leaf as bearer is true.
The blade is sparsely pubescent on the adaxial side. Leaf lamina adaxial epidermis + pubescent is right. 'Sparsely' is only a degree.

fix: In 'A or B to C', the range 'to C' covers the whole alternative set. Keep C as a further value or range end.
reason: The lamina is 'pubescent or pilose to glabrous'. The annotation keeps only pubescent-or-pilose, drops the glabrous end, and so says the lamina is always hairy.
The cymes (inflorescence as container) are many-flowered: flowers present, amount 'many'.
Sepals are glabrous on the adaxial side, so sepal adaxial epidermis is right.
There are 6 perianth segments, which are tepals in Lauraceae. The statement sits under 'Male flowers', but Litsea female flowers also have 6, so the claim holds without the context.
Leaves are sessile or shortly petiolate, given as alternatives.
Leaflets are appressed-pubescent beneath. PO has no leaflet abaxial epidermis, and leaf abaxial epidermis covers it. 'Appressed' is only a hair direction.

fix: When a count word follows a qualified part ('Ray florets numerous', 'Disk florets many'), keep the qualifier in the bearer. PO has ray flower and disc flower.
reason: The flora says ray florets are numerous, not flowers in general. Ray flower (ray floret) exists in PO.
There are 4–6 ovules per locule, with locule (PO_0025263) as the container.
'Unwinged' is winged, negated, on the stem.
There are 1–2 flowers per axil.
The petiole is very slightly winged by decurrent blade tissue.

fix: 'Almost leafless', 'nearly leafless' and 'subaphyllous' mean leaves are few or reduced. Do not read them as absence. Only a bare '-less' with no 'almost/nearly/sub-' is absence.
reason: 'Almost leafless' says leaves are few or small, not missing. Negated presence makes the plant leafless, which the flora does not say.

target: ovary + pedicel together (no single PO term)
fix: 'Ovary and pedicel N mm' (common in orchids) is one length for the two parts together. Do not give it to either part alone. Skip it or use a combined bearer.
reason: 4–6 mm is the length of the ovary and pedicel together, not of the pedicel alone.
Bracteoles of male flowers are 5–8 mm long, with male flower as the whole. The first number of 'L x W' is the length.
Seeds are suborbicular in outline, which is orbicular, approximately.

target: corolla tube (PO_0025166 if present) with position base
fix: In 'inserted at base of X', the target is X (here the corolla tube) at its base. Do not use a generic 'plant organ base' with X dropped.
reason: The stamens are inserted at the base of the corolla tube. The target is only a generic 'plant organ base', which loses the corolla tube the statement is about.
'Anthers not exserted' is exserted, negated, on the anther.

fix: When a negation is followed by a direction plus a quality ('not laterally compressed', 'not dorsally flattened'), negate the directional quality. Negating the general one says more than the flora does.
reason: The flora denies only lateral compression. Negating plain 'condensed' (compressed) says the achene body is not compressed in any direction. PATO has laterally compressed.
